condition_note: Subgrades of 10 for Centering and 9.5 for Surface.
special_note: Includes birthdate inscriptions for both players.
description_block:
When you look back on sports icons of the last 30 years, few come close to the level of influence, fame and admiration as LeBron James and Tiger Woods. Both are among the very best to play their respective sports, James in basketball and Woods in golf. Both have the pedigree of timeless legends. They're champions at the highest levels. They hold numerous records. They've help shape the next generation of stars.

Both have been Upper Deck spokesmen for much of their pro careers. Despite this, James and Woods have just three cards that their signatures have appeared together on. Of those, this is the only signature memorabilia card.

This 2009-10 Upper Deck Exquisite Collection Basketball Numbers autographed patch card connects the duo not by sponsorship deals but by their birthdays instead. Each is represented with a swatch worn by Woods in a tournament and James in an NBA game. LeBron's piece has four colors and spells out the middle part of ""Cleveland."" These are displayed in a window that reads 30—the day in December both were born.

The signatures, both of which are on-card, have been assessed as 10s by BGS. They also come with birthdate inscriptions, ""12-30-84"" for James and ""12-30-75"" for Woods.

Numbered 2/3, the card is graded a NM-MT+ by BGS and includes subgrades of 10 for Centering and 9.5 for Surface.

Needless to say, this is one of the most impressive combinations for any Exquisite Collection card, a game-changing brand that represents the very best in sports cards.

card_name: 2003 Topps Chrome Gold Refractor LeBron James ROOKIE
special_note: Matches LeBron's jersey number during his time in Miami and winning three Olympic gold medals.
description_block:
Before LeBron James arrived in Cleveland, the Cavaliers and the Detroit Pistons did not have an intense rivalry, but Topps seemingly predicted the future when producing LeBron’s 2003-04 Topps Chrome rookie card. As LeBron developed, the teams became fierce Eastern Conference foes, and he took some of his first shots in the budding rivalry during a preseason game on October 7, 2003. Allen Einstein, Detroit’s team photographer, captured an image of LeBron shooting a jumper over Ben Wallace during that game, and Topps used it for LeBron’s revered Chrome rookie card. Topps gave the rookies more appeal in the Chrome set by updating the photos, giving most of them NBA action shots instead of the draft night or college photos found on most rookie cards in the flagship Topps set. 

The shot of LeBron’s shot over Wallace remains one of the most enduring images of LeBron’s illustrious cardboard career. And that reverence is only enhanced by the addition of the stunning Gold Refractor shine. Numbered /50, it is the rarest parallel for one of The King's crowning rookie cards outside of four different 1/1 Printing Plates. The 2003-04 Topps Chrome Gold Refractor LeBron James simply doesn't surface for sale publicly very often. 

This particular copy has the added significance of being copy 06/50. This matches the jersey number James wore during his time in Miami as well as winning three Olympic gold medals for USA Basketball.

It's also one of just nine copies to carry a Gem Mint 10 grade from PSA.

special_note: First rookie in MLB history to hit four home runs in one game.
description_block:
In 2023, Topps introduced one of the most exciting new products in recent memory – MLB Rookie Debut Patch Autographs. While RPAs have long been intriguing prospects for collectors, these cards feature a special MLB DEBUT patch taken directly from the sleeve of the jersey a player wears in his first big-league game. Unsurprisingly, the 1/1 masterpieces proved to be a massive hit, prompting Topps to once again produce the cards for its ensuing Chrome Update sets.

Nick Kurtz is arguably the top card from the 2025 Topps Chrome Update MLB Debut Patch Autograph crop. The 2025 American League Rookie of the Year, Kurtz hit 36 home runs in his first season with the Athletics. His stellar rookie numbers include a .290 bating average, 86 RBI and a 5.4 WAR in 117 games. Among his many 2025 highlights, on July 25, Kurtz hit four home runs in one game making him the first rookie in MLB history to do so. 

With just a single copy, this may be the only time in history to land Kurtz's MLB Debut Patch Autograph. 

The card comes sealed in a Topps holder.

When Shohei Ohtani first signed with the Los Angeles Angels, expectations were high. For virtually everybody alive, the idea of a two-way player was limited to reading stories about Babe Ruth or watching a fielder take to the mound in a blowout. But Ohtani was built differently. He could hit, pitch and field—all at an elite level. Injuries slowed him somewhat for his first couple of seasons but then immortality took hold. Ohtani truly is unlike any player who came before him. Already a two-time World Series Champion, four-time MVP and the founding member of the 50/50 Club, that is really just the beginning of Ohtani's accolades.

In 2013, Panini Creative Director Brandon Lesley contacted Hungarian illustrator Gyula Nemeth to draw the NBA players selected for a 20-card insert for Panini’s Innovation basketball set. Nemeth responded by creating one of the most unforgettable card series in industry history, the stunning pop art collection known as Kaboom! cards. Nemeth portrayed the players as comic book characters, with the reverse side of this card so nice that it could pass as the front. A combination of scarcity, unique typography, original illustrations, and high-flying dunking poses featured on each card in the series made it an instant classic. Kaboom! cards remain beloved – and extremely rare – to this day. Collectors from around the globe chase these case hits each year, with rare parallels such as 1/1 Green eliciting elevated levels of excitement from those lucky to land them.

Randomly inserted into packs at a rate of 1:720, the oval-shaped cards honor the NBA’s best slam dunkers in a 15-card set. The Jordan ranks high on wish lists with its remarkable color scheme, stunning design, and a flip side story reminisces about Jordan taking off from the free throw line in the most epic Slam Dunk Contest in NBA history. The photo of Jordan on this card presents like a king at coronation. Fans obsess over the Jordan Jambalaya—and with good reason.   

During Jordan’s career, MJ dazzled young fans on the court and made time for them when the lights dimmed. Make-A-Wish children facing life-ending diseases visited Michael in the locker room. He would sit with them, listen to their stories, and offer his support. Cheryl Stout, who covered the Bulls for Chicago Public Radio, remembers those moments. “I’ll never forget this little girl. She was maybe about four, and he sat with her and just talked with her. We kept our distance to give them privacy, but we could see the exchange. When they finished, the little girl left, and Michael, tears just came down his face. It was really emotional to see. That’s something that I won’t ever forget.” Michael’s impact on people, especially children, was immeasurable. It is one of the many reasons fans flock to his cards decades after his retirement—and few more so than this rare high-grade Jambalaya.

description_block:
In 1982, Topps decided to cease its basketball card operations. With the end of their monopoly on bubble gum cards allowing Fleer and Donruss to enter the baseball market in 1981, Topps focused its efforts on fending off its newly created competition. Baseball cards were significantly more popular and more profitable than basketball cards at the time—but as the major card producers began churning out baseball sets, NBA fans were left without cards to collect. The Star company released a full basketball set two years later, but with its low print run and limited distribution, 1984-85 Star failed to resurrect the market. Then, Fleer decided to enter the fray. Unable to best the baseball behemoth Topps, the company turned its attention to the hoops market, releasing the iconic 1986-87 Fleer basketball set.  

Unlike Star’s releases, 1986-87 Fleer Basketball had a wider distribution in a more traditional format, with cards sold in standard wax packs as opposed to bagged team sets. Because of the five-year production gap between 1981-82 Topps and 1986-87 Fleer, the set also became the default rookie year release for several iconic rookie draft classes, including the cards of Hall of Famers Hakeem Olajuwon, Karl Malone, Dominique Wilkins, Isiah Thomas, and Patrick Ewing. The set also includes NBA all-timers like Larry Bird, Magic Johnson, and Kareem Abdul-Jabbar. 

But, of course, the ultimate chase card is the 1986-87 Fleer Michael Jordan rookie. This BBCE-authenticated 36-pack box provides a prime opportunity to land an untouched example of this celebrated issue alongside other popular cards, including His Airness' 1986-87 Fleer sticker.

special_note: Limited issue featuring a beautiful three-color game-used patch.
description_block:
Following a heavy-handed 4-1 series loss to the Phoenix Suns in the opening round of the 2007 NBA playoffs, Kobe Bryant had had enough. Lakers management seemed more concerned with beginning a rebuild around the blossoming Andrew Bynum than surrounding Kobe with championship-caliber talent, leading the disgruntled superstar to demand a trade during the ‘07 offseason. “Just so you know, we feel you’re the best player in the world,” then-team president Mitch Kupchak told Bryant. “Any team we talk to, we’re gonna want the best player [in return].” Although that fact certainly threw a wrench in Kobe’s plan to join a contender, teams showed no shortage of interest in trading for the three-time NBA champion. The Mavericks pushed to pair Kobe with the legendary Dirk Nowitzki, and the Bulls reportedly offered an enticing package of Joakim Noah, Luol Deng, Tyrus Thomas, and Ben Gordon. L.A. even considered dealing the “Black Mamba” to Cleveland in exchange for 22-year-old LeBron James (the Cavs shut that one down immediately). Finally, after weeks of negotiations, the Lakers settled on a trade to Detroit, with Kobe heading to the Motor City in exchange for a treasure trove of picks and young players. However, Kobe had not greenlit the Pistons as one of his preferred trade destinations, leading him to enact his no-trade clause and remain in L.A. 

Spurred by Kobe’s unhappiness, the Lakers ultimately traded for All-Star big man Pau Gasol midway through the 2007-08 season. The pair clicked immediately, and after only one season together, Bryant and Gasol led L.A. to back-to-back championships in 2009 and 2010. Just as Lakers fans remain forever grateful that Bryant stuck it out in L.A., the winner of this 2007-08 Upper Deck Exquisite Collection Limited Logos Patch Auto will certainly be glad the “Black Mamba” never traded his signature purple and gold for any other colors. A stunning limited issue featuring a beautiful three-color game-used patch and a hard-signed, 10-grade autograph, this  example could transform any collection into a contender.

Graded a NM-MT+ 8.5 by BGS, this card has also earned Fanatics Collect–A Eye Appeal designation.

special_note: One of Tom Brady's toughest unnumbered rookie cards to pull.
description_block:
Topps released 12 football card sets in 2000 but only included Tom Brady in two, Bowman and Bowman Chrome. This means the legendary quarterback has only a single rookie Refractor. Among the 105 rookies on the Bowman Chrome checklist, Topps serial-numbered base cards of 20 top prospects to /99. That left Brady and 84 other draftees as unnumbered short prints whose Refractors fell 1:281 packs. It took an average of nearly 24,000 packs to uncover a Brady, leaving this card as one of his toughest unnumbered rookie cards to pull.

The photo used on the card and the detailed write-up on the reverse also receive attention from collectors. Of Brady’s 23 rookie cards that depict him with the Patriots, only eight show him in full uniform instead of at practice. Most of those issues show Brady casually warming up for a preseason game, but the Bowman card shows him rolling out of the pocket. On the back, Brady’s “Bowman Briefing” expounds on his baseball pedigree, big-game accomplishments, and the on-field skills that eventually defined his career. Considering Refractors have helped define the trading card industry since 1993, the shine from this issue makes it many collectors' choice to sit atop the list of Tom Brady's best cards.

Every year’s release contained quad relic cards, but Upper Deck produced more of them in 2007-08 than in the past. 

Fifty-nine players signed cards for the Exquisite Extra Quad Jerseys Autograph set. But none of them are as coveted as the one and only Michael Jordan. This example, stamped 07/10, proudly displays four swatches from a Bulls uniform and a 10-grade signature from His Airness, flashing the attributes that make Exquisite one of the defining products of basketball card collecting history.

card_name: Championship Tags LeBron James TAG PATCH
special_note: Represents an important piece of history for both James' career and the Cavaliers franchise.
description_block:
Beginning in 2014-15, the collars of NBA jerseys received a small addition in the form of a championship tag—at least the jerseys for franchises that had won at least one title. These small tags noted the number of championships. They were a nod to history and motivation for the future. When it comes to basketball cards, they also make for impressive memorabilia cards.

This 2024-25 Panini Eminence Championship Tags LeBron James, numbered /3, comes from the latter part of The King's second tenure in Cleveland. He led the Cavs to their only NBA Championship in 2016 before heading to the Lakers for 2018-19. It's both a seldom-seen swatch and one that represents an important piece of history for both James' career and the Cavaliers franchise.

It also comes from Eminence, a special product that appears when Panini sees fit. It's meant to be the ultimate in luxury at every turn, even higher than National Treasures and Flawless. As one of the NBA's all-time greats who also happens to have won four championships, James certainly fits.

This card comes in a sealed Eminence holder from Panini.

special_note: Redemption card for a limited edition Gold Logoman Patch.
description_block:
After launching in baseball, the Gold Logoman patch concept made the jump to hoops with 2025-26 Topps Chrome Basketball. These jersey patches are worn exclusively by the NBA's top award winners from the 2024-25 season: MVP, Defensive Player of the Year and Rookie of the Year. No other players got these patches. The result is special and extremely limited cards for a very select few players.

Stephon Castle made it back-to-back ROY wins for the San Antonio Spurs after Victor Wembanyama won the award the previous season. The fourth overall pick in the 2024 draft, Castle averaged 14.7 points and 4.1 assists per game in his debut season with the Spurs. He's improved on that so far in 2025-26 and, more importantly, has helped the Spurs get near the top of the Western Conference standings.

While there is already plenty of prestige behind these cards, it's worth noting that baseball has two winners for each award, one for the American League and one for the National League. The NBA has just three total Gold Logoman recipients.

The winner of this auction receives an unused and unscratched redemption card for Castle's Gold Logoman Patch card from 2025-26 Topps Chrome Basketball. They will be free to redeem it and have it sent to them as soon as the card is made. The final patch card will be numbered /4.

Two years after fulfilling that promise, LeBron took his career to Los Angeles to etch his name into the storied history of the Lakers franchise. By moving to California, he earned legions of new fans, and collectors flocked to 2018-19 releases to find LeBron’s first Lakers cards.

The Gold Prizm has remained a familiar staple within the brand since its debut in 2012-13, and this PSA 10 example of LeBron’s first /10 Gold Prizm listed as a member of the Lakers is arguably the most coveted non-rookie on the 300-card checklist. He brought L.A. its 17th championship in his second season on the West Coast, surpassed Kareem Abdul-Jabbar as the all-time leading scorer in NBA history in 2023, and has not shared any retirement plans despite already logging two decades in the league—making his Lakers chapter just as memorable as the other segments of his career.

Exquisite Enshrinements debuted in 2004-05, the second year of Exquisite, bringing a clean, elegant design that allowed subjects such as Michael Jordan—and their autographs—to shine. 

This card from the 2006-07 release showcases a regal design with plenty of room to highlight both His Airness and his signature. And this PSA Authentic example’s 23/25 serial number adds an extra layer of intrigue thanks to Jordan’s famous jersey number.

Ohtani came to Major League Baseball with massive hype in December 2017, and a burning question in trading card circles early in 2018 surrounded when his first rookies would appear in packs. One of his first appearances came in 2018 Bowman, and collectors could not wait to try to uncover examples of his “1st Bowman” Chrome Rookie Autograph card. Featuring a photo of Ohtani following through on his windup, his hard-signed autograph has a slate of eight parallels, including this vibrant Green /99. After six seasons and two MVP awards with the Angels, Ohtani moved to the Dodgers ahead of the 2024 season. With the megastar going on to win both the N.L. MVP and World Series in 2024 and 2025, and establishing the 50/50 Club, it appears to have been the right move for him.

Lionel Messi was an otherworldly talent from the jump, though you do not have to travel to outer space to land a card as out of this world as this 2004 Mundi Cromo Liga rookie. While the Argentine icon’s 2004-05 Mega Cracks is widely regarded as his premier first-year card, this Spanish issue is technically Messi’s earliest soccer release.

special_note: Low-numbered parallels of Michael Jordan always draw attention.
description_block:
Low-numbered parallels of Michael Jordan always draw attention, and the Ultra Platinum Medallion is certainly in that class. Featuring Michael in a gravity-defying moment, the Ultra shows him in his original Chicago colorway Air Jordan I’s—the classic red, white, and black shoe—that he had originally worn back in 1984.  

In the Last Dance documentary, Jordan reminisced about his desire to play his last game in Madison Square Garden in the original shoe. While His Airness was uncomfortable in the antiquated Jordan I’s, he did not feel he could remove them because he was having such a good game. He scored a memorable 42 points as the Bulls beat the Knicks 102-89. When Jordan finally unlaced the shoes, his socks were covered in blood. Whether the shoe was a size small, or he had acclimated to the more comfortable versions developed in the 14 years since he first wore them is unclear—perhaps both. But what is not debatable is that Jordan always turned it up for Spike Lee and the New York fans. 

This pop 3 Mint PSA 9, stamped 04/99, turns it up for Jordan collectors who appreciate playing-day issues that are hard to locate due to His Airness' immense popularity.

The certification number on this card has been checked against the third-party grader's online database and is active as of 01/08/2026.

special_note: This card is part of a limited hand-numbered series and features a high-grade autograph.
description_block:
Jack Silverstein had a plan. As a college student in 1999, the future sports historian and author did not have enough money to purchase season tickets to watch his beloved Chicago Bulls. Instead, he put himself on the wait list because he figured he would finish his education and have a job by the time he reached the top. But after the Bulls traded Scottie Pippen, traded Steve Kerr, released Dennis Rodman, and—most significantly—Michael Jordan retired, the excitement in Chicago’s fanbase quickly dissipated. 

“A year later, I get a call,” Silverstein recalled. “It’s the Bulls’ season-ticket office: ‘We’re excited to tell you you’ve come to the top of the season-ticket waitlist.’ I was like, ‘No! That’s not the plan!’ People getting rid of their season tickets was a sign of how fast the bottom fell out.” 

Jordan’s retirement in January rocked a league already reeling from a prolonged lockout that delayed the start of the 1998-99 season, and the ensuing moves by the Bulls dropped them from the league’s best to one of the league’s worst. Without Jordan, the Bulls finished last in the Eastern Conference standings for four straight years, and they have yet to return to the NBA Finals. 

But as the six-time champion left the league, tributes poured in worldwide, including from Upper Deck. The company produced several sets dedicated to Jordan’s career following his retirement, including the Michael Jordan Athlete of the Century offering. Upper Deck packaged the 90-card set in packs and boxes, and a handful of lucky collectors uncovered one of the two autographs from the series. Two hard-signed cards from the product highlight the release, and collectors rarely find the hand-numbered /23 offerings available on the open market. This month’s Premier Auction presents one of his scarce Superstar Signatures autographs (#MJSS1), and collectors will not likely want to waitlist their chance to acquire it.

Although this card has not received a numerical grade, it has been authenticated by PSA. The autograph has been assessed as a 10.

The certification number on this card has been checked against the third-party grader's online database and is active as of 01/08/2026.

description_block:
1997 SPx Bsaketball was released on the heels of the 1997 NBA playoffs, months after Kobe Bryant wrapped up his rookie season. As stated on the back of his card #21, the Lakers youngster had shown flashes of All-Star potential in that debut campaign. Those flashes, of course, ignited a full-blown Hall of Fame career, with Mamba becoming one of the most beloved players to ever take the court. 

This Upper Deck SPx Grand Finale parallel portrays a young Bryant dunking, with the beautiful foil die-cut design of the /50 printing only enhancing that imagery. 

When Upper Deck debuted the SPx brand with baseball in 1996, it was all about cutting-edge technology. The most noticeable was its use of holograms but there were also foil accents and die-cut designs. These principles carried over to other sports for the next couple of years. Although SPx continued to push the limits of technology and sports cards, Upper Deck decided to shift away from the hologram process the called Holoview. Enter the Grand Finale parallel, a send off of sorts commemorating the change.

Highly condition-sensitive thanks to that design, these prized pieces are tough to track down in quality condition. As such, this PSA 7 Kobe is a pop 5 with only two graded higher.

special_note: Iconic card, significant historical importance in basketball card collecting.
description_block:
In 1986, Fleer, which had been out of the basketball card business since 1961, inked a deal with the NBA to manufacture basketball cards. The company’s return to hoops became arguably the most famous card set in hardwood history—largely thanks to card #57, the Michael Jordan rookie card.

As Michael Jordan’s career unfolded, he generated interest in the set, which featured this wildly attractive card that perfectly captured one of his signature moves with his tongue out in full force. Fleer had the vision to use an action shot of the NCAA champion out of UNC, though nobody could have possibly predicted the height of his NBA success. The card is buoyed by not having any mainstream competition from other companies like Topps. As long as there are basketball card collectors, there will always be interest in this card.

Of the more than 14,750 times that BGS has assessed this card, only 550 have achieved a Gem Mint 9.5 grade with just six ranking higher. With a 10 subgrade for Centering and 9.5 for Corners, Surface and Edges, this copy achieves True Gem status, making it one of the top condition copies in existence.

Lionel Messi was an otherworldly talent from the get-go, though collectors will not have to catch a spaceship to land a card as out of this world as this 2004 Panini Sports Mega Cracks Barca Campio rookie. While the Argentine icon’s ‘04 Mega Cracks La Liga is often hailed as his premier first-year card, this Catalan issue also holds a unique place in Messi’s rookie catalog. For the 2004-05 La Liga season, Panini produced two Barcelona team sets, with one version being Spanish (“Barca Campeón”) and the other Catalan (“Barca Campio”). While it is common for Catalan speakers to be fluent in Spanish, the reverse is not necessarily the case. For this reason, the Spanish version of this card proved more popular than its Catalan counterpart, though this has only made high-grade examples of the latter all the rarer. Of the more than 560 Campio examples assessed by PSA, this is one of only nine to earn a coveted PSA 10 grade. We all know what Messi became in the years that followed the release of this printing. But when it comes to this Barca Campio rookie, there is truly no telling what heights it might one day reach.

Drake Maye has quickly emerged as one of the most exciting young prospects in the NFL. Drafted in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft, Maye brought with him a strong college résumé from North Carolina, where he showcased a powerful arm, poise in the pocket, and impressive athleticism. In his rookie season, he flashed the tools that made scouts so high on him—tight-window throws and the ability to extend plays with his legs. What sets Maye apart from some of his peers is his combination of size, mobility, and natural feel for the game. With a sophomore season that's made him one of the favorites to win the league's MVP, he’s shown early signs of leadership and resilience, traits that point toward a bright future as a franchise quarterback. Understandably, this has increased the outlook on his top rookie cards.

This 2024 Panini National Treasures Tremendous Treasures Tag Drake Maye is one of his top cards. The 1/1 has an oversized tag swatch as the centerpiece. It features both an NFL Shield logo and Nike Swoosh.

James' 2003-04 Topps 1st Edition rookie card looks almost identical to his iconic flagship Topps rookie card. It has the same photo and the same design. The giveaway is the jersey. When Jordan came out of retirement in March, 1995, it meant that all card manufacturers could make basketball cards of the legend once again. Topps rushed to make a card for Finest Series 2, an odd-numbered bookend at #331. This variation has Jordan wearing a 23 jersey. However, the much more common final version of the card has His Airness sporting the number 45, what he wore for a short time upon his return.

While the exact origins of this card are not known, it appears to be a production sample. Besides the jersey, the diagonal on the front coating are not typical for regular cards. On the back, the variation is missing ""Skin Protector Pat. Pending"" under the copyright info. It's on the regular version of the card. Based on sheets that have surfaced for 1994-95 Finest, Jordan was printed separately from the other Series 2 cards, likely because production was so far along when he made his return.

description_block:
The NBA’s landscape changed dramatically in 1979 when a pair of clean-cut rookies broke into the league and brokered a new era that turned into one of the greatest rivalries in league history. The two rookies stormed onto the scene, putting their skills next to living legends like Julius Erving and Kareem Abdul-Jabbar. But more importantly, Larry Bird and Magic Johnson each brought their own brand to the NBA, giving the league sturdy marketing pillars that helped fill arenas across the country.

Three times, Magic’s Lakers and Bird’s Celtics matched up for the title, but despite that fierce competition, the duo became friends later in life and continue to serve as stewards of the game.

Just as Larry and Magic forever altered the NBA, Topps changed the basketball card landscape in 1980, delivering a new style of base card for its flagship set—and printing one of the most iconic NBA cards of all time. Throughout its history in the basketball card industry, Topps had tinkered with the design and size of its base cards. In 1980, the company issued standard-sized cards, but each card served as a perforated three-card panel, essentially giving collectors three cards for the price of one. Of the many tri-panels offered in the set, none holds more prestige than the one featuring rookie cards of Bird and Magic on either side of Erving’s “Scoring Leader” offering. description_block:
Before LeBron James arrived in Cleveland, the Cavaliers and the Detroit Pistons did not have an intense rivalry, but Topps seemed to look into its crystal ball to bring attention to the future when producing LeBron’s 2003 Topps Chrome rookie card. As LeBron developed, the teams became fierce Eastern Conference foes, and LeBron took some of his first shots in the budding rivalry during a preseason game on October 7, 2003. Allen Einstein, Detroit’s team photographer, captured an image of LeBron taking a jump shot over Ben Wallace during that game, and Topps used it for LeBron’s revered Chrome rookie card. This example of his 2003-04 Topps Chrome X-Fractor gives collectors a perfect reminder of the rivalry that helped LeBron establish himself as one of the NBA’s best players. 

X-Fractors, first produced in baseball and football in 2001, place the reflective Refractor effect throughout a checkboard pattern across the front of the card in an enhanced design. They're reminiscent of late 1990s Atomic Refractors. The technology first appeared in basketball sets during LeBron’s rookie year. Each box of Topps Chrome contained a special silver pack that included one encased and uncirculated /220 X-Fractor parallel from the 165-card set, leaving collectors with long-shot odds of finding any specific player (1:177 boxes when factoring in foreign language rookie variations). But unlike every other Refractor parallel from 2003, the odds of pulling a rookie’s X-Fractor were equal to the odds of pulling a veteran (e.g., veteran Black Refractors are unnumbered and had stated odds of 1:18 packs, while rookie Black Refractors are /500). 

James' Topps Chrome rookie recognizes his brilliant high school career and standing as the No. 1 pick in the 2003 draft, and it remains the most coveted card from a star-studded rookie checklist. In the Chrome set, Topps gave the rookies more appeal by updating the photos, giving most of them NBA action shots as opposed to the draft night or college photos found on most rookie cards in the flagship Topps set. That dynamic imagery is joined by the now-famous lustrous checkerboard finish.

This Mint BGS 9 includes 9.5 subgrades for Corners, Surface and Edges.

description_block:
The Simpsons is one of the most iconic television series in history. On the air since December, 1989 (longer if you count the shorts on The Tracey Ullman Show), the exploits of Homer, Marge, Bart, Lisa, Maggie and the rest of Springfield have entertained multiple generations. The show's impact on pop culture cannot be understated.

Only a handful of trading card sets have been produced for the show over the years with 1993 SkyBox Simpsons being one of the most important. While there are lots of fun elements on the checklist, it's a single card that carries a lot of the clout, which is understandable given the fact that it's one of the most important entertainment trading cards ever produced. Inside packs were 400 total Art DeBart redemption cards. Each was good for a sketch card with original art. The concept is common today but it was in its infancy in 1993. However, unlike modern sketch cards that use large rosters of artists, often numbering more than 100, Art DeBart had one. It just so happened to be Matt Groening, the creator of The Simpsons.

So each of these sketch cards are original pieces of art drawn and signed by the person who came up with one of the most impact TV shows ever. The 1993 SkyBox Art DeBart cards are art, autographs and history all mixed into one.

While there are 400 total in existence, there is some variation that makes a lot of these unique. Bart Simpson is the most common character on these, but even those can change things up. Originally known for its foil-splashed “Premier Prospects” rookie cards, SP’s approach to rookies changed in 1997 when Upper Deck adopted the SP Authentic branding as the product became home to numerous autograph sets. description_block:
In 1998, the Metal Universe design took an approach that paid tribute to the set’s roots as Fleer Metal. Using silver foil, the new design was a significant deviation from the Marvel-themed 1997 checklist and the cityscape-based 1997 Championship Edition sets that collectors still love today. In 1998, Fleer/SkyBox gave its Metal Universe cards an actual metal appearance by printing embossed foil nameplates that appear to be forged from steel and riveted into the card. Fleer/SkyBox covered the 123 player cards with a refractive golden finish and a limited production to only /50 for the PMG parallel.

Collectors widely rank PMGs among the most iconic parallels ever produced. The set was conceived from Fleer/SkyBox’s desire to design cards differently from other manufacturers. “If you could take a design and make it pop by doing physical applications to the cardboard, that’s what really drove a set, from a design quality standpoint,” recalled Jeff Massien, who served as Fleer’s President and COO in the early 1990s and coined the company’s internal “Different by Design” slogan. “You couldn’t overdesign a card, as long as the player remained in the foreground. You can’t overglitz it. So, that’s what we did.” Every year, the Metal Universe checklist was filled with condition-sensitive cards because of the full-bleed designs, so any time collectors find any example of a PMG, especially one featuring a superstar of Dennis Rodman's caliber, there is reason for excitement.

One can't overlook the aesthetic appeal gold brings to Curry cards, offering a team color match that goes perfectly with his uniform. Simply put, in addition to the the prestige and history this card brings, it's a visual stunner.

special_note: This card commemorates Michael Jordan's 35th birthday and his performance during the 1997-98 NBA season.
description_block:
The 1997-98 season was an important one in NBA history. The Bulls were set to win their third straight NBA title, and a 35-year-old Michael Jordan was cementing his legacy of going a perfect 6-0 in the NBA Finals. On February 17, 1998—MJ’s 35th birthday—the Bulls played a home game against the Indiana Pacers, foreshadowing the Eastern Conference Finals. Michael had—for Michael--a relatively pedestrian 27 points, shooting an accurate 13/23 from the field. The Pacers, led by Reggie Miller’s 34 points, could not keep up with the more physical Bulls on the glass, getting outrebounded 42-26. The ultimate result, a 105-97 victory for the Bulls, was Jordan’s birthday present to himself, though the Chicago home crowd probably enjoyed it as well.  

This rarely-seen UD MJx Autographs card hearkens back to that historic season. With fragile all-black card stock, this BGS 8.5 /50 presents nicely. The blue-penned signature pairs beautifully with the dual images of the Bulls superstar in his prime.

For this Gem Mint PSA 10 Victor Wembanyama, it channels his nickname, The Alien. Chilling on a flying saucer, the top pick in the 2023 NBA Draft is depicted calm and cool. Without any autographs in NBA products for his first two seasons, this is easily one of Wemby's top sophomore releases. 

In fact, Panini Prizm Black Manga has proven to be one of the most sought after inserts among all 2024-25 basketball card releases.

description_block:
Metal Universe is one of the seminal sports card brands of the late 1990s. Flamboyant, eye-catching designs were a hallmark each year, closing out the decade with embossed foil as the defining feature. All 300 cards in the 1999 Metal Universe base set came with two parallels, Precious Metal Gems that are /50 and 1/1 Gem Masters. 

At the time, 1/1 cards were still relatively innovative, having debuted just a couple of years earlier. A lot of sets still didn’t include them, which makes any such printing, much less one of one of the best pitchers of the era, all the more enticing today.

Curt Schilling was not just one of the best pitchers of his generation, but he knew how to come through in the biggest situations. In the Netflix Redeem Team documentary, LeBron James and Dwyane Wade speak about the impact of Kobe Bryant. When Mamba arrived at training camp in Las Vegas, he was all business. There had been a party that went into the wee hours, and as the players returned to the hotel at 5 am, they ran into Kobe, who was heading to the gym to work out before morning practice. The players were initially surprised, if not amused, but after a few days of Kobe’s intensity at practice, the other team leaders—LeBron, Wade, and Carmelo Anthony—began to join him for morning weightlifting and other conditioning. Bryant raised the level of Team USA, positively impacting their eventual success in Beijing. 

Similarly, Fleer helped raise the level of insert cards in the 1990s, and this /100 1999-00 Fleer Mystique Raise the Roof Kobe Bryant is one shining example. As the Lakers legend soars, the attractive surface and multiple images create a mystical vibe that positively impacts its visual appeal. Simply put, this is one of the key Kobe inserts.

That year, the company’s creative director, Brandon Lesley, teamed up with Hungarian illustrator Gyula Nemeth for a new 20-card insert set called Kaboom!. Nemeth illustrated the players in a pop art style, and Panini backed his artwork with eccentric foil patterns and inserted the cards as case hits in the Panini Innovation set. Basketball collectors fell in love with Kaboom! cards, so Panini did not take long to print them for other sports, including 2018’s multi-sport checklist that gave a handful of NFL players their first Kaboom! card. Panini released the first standalone NFL Kaboom! set in 2019, and football collectors have highly regarded the rare inserts ever since.

The 2025 Panini Absolute Kaboom! set once again offered collectors Horizontal and Vertical cards as well as Gold /10 and Green 1/1 parallels. A crucial piece of the annual hunt for superstar quarterbacks' best cards, collectors eagerly chase Kaboom! cards of players with the pedigree of Josh Allen.

special_note: Iconic 1952 Bowman issue, significant for collectors of Mickey Mantle.
description_block:
The resilient Bowman would not be outdone as they battled Topps for popularity in the early 1950s. Their designers kept pace with the iconic 1952 Bowman issue, which offers collectors another gem as a follow-up to the Mantle ‘51 Bowman rookie issue. The intense look on Mantle’s face as he gazes into the distance captures the intensity with which he played the game during his first season.

When Mantle joined the Yankees in 1951, he struggled at the plate, going 0-22 out of the gate. When Stengel sent him back to AA ball for the Kansas City Blues to work on his swing, he did not know if he would return. Hailed as DiMaggio’s successor, Mantle felt the pressure to perform. It did not help that DiMaggio did not lay out the red carpet. Stengel eventually moved Mantle from the infield to right field to relieve some of the pressure on him. Mantle’s first year presented its share of challenges: threats and hurled items in his direction from opposing fans, scurrilous New York businessmen seeking to fleece him, accusations of dodging the Korean War, and the temptations of a big city for a 19-year-old kid from Oklahoma. He made it anyway.

This NM-MT 8 is one of the top copies of the card in the PSA registry. Of the more than 4,200 times the company has assessed this card, just 21 rank higher.

Messi made his official (aka not exhibition) Barcelona senior team debut at age 17 on October 16, 2004, against Espanyol. When he stepped on the field as a sub in the 82nd minute, he became the youngest player to appear for the Catalan giants in an official match. That began a glittering 17 seasons in one of the most famous sides in soccer history. 

The 2004 Mega Cracks card is a fitting first for Messi. The issue, only released in Spain, is difficult to find in top condition due to poor card stock and a perceived lack of care taken by European collectors in the early 2000s. With Messi's legacy cemented, it has also become one of the undisputed icons in 2000s sports card collecting.

This particular card is extra special. It includes an aftermarket Lionel Messi autograph, a 10 as assessed by PSA/DNA. Signed in blue ink, the stunning signature runs through the center of the card. Just eight autographed copies rank higher than this PSA 4.5 card. This card has also earned Fanatics Collect–E Eye Appeal designation.
